# StringView

A borrowed run of bytes that has been checked to be UTF-8.

```rux
pub struct StringView {
    // private fields
}
```

Copy, owning nothing. The bytes it names must outlive it.

## Constructors

<h3 id="new"><code>StringView</code></h3>

```rux
pub func StringView() -> StringView
```

A view over nothing.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: an empty view

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L27)

## Associated functions

<h3 id="from-bytes"><code>FromBytes</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FromBytes(bytes: char8[..]) -> StringView?
```

A view over `bytes` when they are UTF-8, and `none` when they are not.
`bytes` is borrowed and must outlive the view. This is the only way to make a view out of bytes whose
provenance is unknown, and it costs one pass over them.
Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing.

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |

**Returns**: a view over those bytes, or `none` when they are not valid UTF-8

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L38)

<h3 id="from-validated"><code>FromValidated</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FromValidated(bytes: char8[..]) -> StringView
```

A view over bytes the caller vouches are UTF-8.
Skips the pass [`FromBytes`](/docs/api/text/string-view#from-bytes) makes, which is worth having when the bytes came from something that already
guarantees it — another view, a [`String`](/docs/api/text/string), a literal.
The bytes must be well-formed UTF-8. Everything downstream assumes it, so bytes that are not produce wrong
answers rather than errors: a scalar walk reads past a truncated sequence, and a cut lands mid-character.

| Name    | Type        | Description         |
| ------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
| `bytes` | `char8[..]` | the bytes to act on |

**Returns**: a view over those bytes, taken as valid without checking

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L51)

<h3 id="index-of"><code>IndexOf</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IndexOf(
    self: &StringView,
    needle: StringView
) -> uint?
```

The byte index where `needle` first occurs, or `none`.
The empty needle occurs at the start, which is what makes `IndexOf` agree with [`StartsWith`](/docs/api/text/string-view#starts-with) for it.
Runs in time proportional to the product of the lengths in the worst case, which for the short needles this
is used with is the same as proportional to the text.

| Name     | Type         | Description          |
| -------- | ------------ | -------------------- |
| `needle` | `StringView` | the text to look for |

**Returns**: the byte offset of the first occurrence, or `none`

<h3 id="part"><code>Part</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Part(
    self: &StringView,
    start: uint,
    end: uint
) -> StringView?
```

The part of this view from `start` up to `end`, or `none` when either is not a boundary or they are the
wrong way round.
Half-open, so `Part(a, b)` and `Part(b, c)` together are `Part(a, c)`. Refusing a cut that is not on a
boundary is the point: the alternative is a view whose first bytes are the tail of a character.
Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

| Name    | Type   | Description                                  |
| ------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `start` | `uint` | the first byte offset, inclusive             |
| `end`   | `uint` | the byte offset one past the last, exclusive |

**Returns**: the text between the two offsets, or `none` when either is not a boundary

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L102)

```rux
    self: &StringView,
    other: &StringView
) -> bool
```

Whether two views hold the same bytes.
Byte equality, which for well-formed UTF-8 is scalar-by-scalar equality, since each scalar value has exactly
one encoding. It is not equality after normalization, which is a different question and a different package.

| ------- | ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `&StringView` | the value to compare against |

<h3 id="compare"><code>Compare</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Compare(
    self: &StringView,
    other: &StringView
) -> Ordering
```

How this view orders against `other`, shortest first where one is a prefix of the other.
Byte order, which for UTF-8 is also code point order: the encoding is built so that comparing bytes and
comparing scalar values give the same answer. It is not alphabetical in any language.

| Name    | Type          | Description                  |
| ------- | ------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `other` | `&StringView` | the value to compare against |

**Returns**: how the two order byte by byte, which is code-point order for UTF-8

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L142)

## Implements Display

`StringView` conforms to [`Display`](/docs/api/text/display).

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(
    self: &StringView,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes what this view spans, truncated to the spec's precision and padded to its width.
Precision counts Unicode scalar values rather than bytes, and a cut lands on a character boundary by
construction: the walk that counts them is the walk that finds where to stop.
Reports whatever the writer reported, and `UnsupportedRequest` for a style, since text has none.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the view's text was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L50)

## Implements Debug

`StringView` conforms to [`Debug`](/docs/api/text/debug).

<h3 id="write-debug"><code>WriteDebug</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDebug(
    self: &StringView,
    writer: &var TextWriter,
    spec: FormatSpec
) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes what this view spans, quoted and escaped.
The quotes sit outside the precision: what is kept is text, and the quotes say where it stops. Alignment is
not applied, because padding a quoted rendering to a width would put the fill outside the quotes, where it
would read as part of the surrounding text rather than as part of the value.
Reports whatever the writer reported, stopping at the first refusal, so a failed opening quote is not
followed by a body. Reports `UnsupportedRequest` for a style.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the quoted view was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/StringView.rux#L67)

<h3 id="is-ascii-space"><code>IsAsciiSpace</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsAsciiSpace(byte: char8) -> bool
```

Whether `byte` is ASCII whitespace: space, tab, newline, carriage return, form feed or vertical tab.
ASCII only, deliberately. Unicode calls a good many more characters whitespace, and which ones is a question for
the tables; every one of them is multi-byte, so trimming by this rule never cuts a character in half.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Search.rux#L162)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type    | Description |
| ------ | ------- | ----------- |
| `byte` | `char8` | the byte    |

**Returns**: whether the byte is one of ASCII's five space characters

A walk over the parts of a view between occurrences of a separator.

**Implements Iterator**

`SplitIterator` conforms to `Iterator`.

<h4 id="split-iterator-next"><code>Next</code></h4>

```rux
pub func Next(self: &var SplitIterator) -> StringView?
```

The next part, or `none` when the walk is over.
Two adjacent separators give an empty part between them, and a separator at either end gives an empty part
there — so the parts always number one more than the separators, and joining them back with the separator
gives what was split. An empty separator gives the whole view as one part, since anything else would be an
endless walk.

**Returns**: the next piece, or `none` at the end

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Text/Src/Search.rux#L188)

The next scalar value, or `none` at the end.
Bytes that are not well-formed end the walk rather than being reported: a view is validated when it is made,
so reaching one means the bytes were vouched for and were not.
